newsitem.title: CHINA: China industrial workforce reduced in first half.
newsitem.headline: China industrial workforce reduced in first half.

text.p: The size of China's industrial workforce decreased in the first half of the year and the state sector accounted for a big part of the reduction, the Business Weekly said on Sunday.
The newspaper said the total number of industrial workers was 146.9 million at the end of June, down 538,000 from the end of the first quarter and down 2.17 million from the end of last year.
Employment at state enterprises was cut by 1.14 million jobs, it said.
China has been trying to restructure ailing state industry, pushing it to trim its bloated workforce and cut costs.

"Such industrial sectors as manufacturing, mining and drilling as well as construction were among the hardest hit by the sharp downturn in the workforce," the newspaper quoted Zhang Jinsheng, a senior researcher at the Ministry of Labour, as saying.
Zhang said that in addition to restructuring delays in construction projects also contributed to the decline.
He said that there might be a moderate rebound in the employment by the year-end due to recent cuts in interest rates, which should spur economic activity.
